A conceptual diagram showing the colonial extractive economy. A large map of Nigeria on the left has arrows pointing outward carrying "Raw Materials (Palm oil, Cocoa, Groundnut, Tin)" towards a factory in Great Britain on the right. Another set of arrows points back from Great Britain to Nigeria carrying "Manufactured Goods (Textiles, Soap, Machinery)".

A map of colonial Nigeria showing the railway network. Two main lines run from the coast to the north. The Western line goes from Lagos through Ibadan, Ilorin, and Minna to Kano. The Eastern line goes from Port Harcourt through Enugu and Makurdi to Kaduna, where it joins the Western line. Dotted lines representing feeder roads branch off from the railway stations into the surrounding areas.
